lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Concept model B: establishing the AA criterion

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Compare these two examples. Find the step where they stop being the same.

items.prompt: Dilate (3, −2) about the origin by factor 4.
A side of 5 becomes 15. Scale factor and area change?

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching parent. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: Triangle ABC has ∠A = 42° and ∠B = 98°. Triangle DEF has ∠D = 42° and ∠E = 98°. Are the triangles similar, and on what grounds?
choices: No; angle information alone never establishes similarity.
Yes, by SSS similarity.
Yes, by AA similarity: two pairs of congruent angles force the third pair to be congruent as well.
Yes, but only if a pair of corresponding sides is also known to be congruent.

items.prompt: Under a dilation, a line that passes through the centre of dilation …
choices: is mapped to a parallel line a fixed distance away
is mapped to a line through the origin with a different slope
is mapped onto itself
is mapped to a perpendicular line

items.prompt: Dilate the point (5, -6) about the origin with scale factor 2. Give the image.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A figure is dilated so that a side of length 2 becomes a side of length 6. What is the scale factor, and what happens to the figure's area?
choices: scale factor 4; the area is multiplied by 9
scale factor 3; the area is multiplied by 9
scale factor 3; the area is multiplied by 3
scale factor 1/3; the area is multiplied by 9

items.prompt: Triangle ABC has ∠A = 32° and ∠B = 48°. Triangle DEF has ∠D = 32° and ∠E = 48°. Are the triangles similar, and on what grounds?
choices: Yes, by SSS similarity.
Yes, but only if a pair of corresponding sides is also known to be congruent.
Yes, by AA similarity: two pairs of congruent angles force the third pair to be congruent as well.
No; angle information alone never establishes similarity.

items.prompt: Under a dilation, a line that does not pass through the centre of dilation …
choices: is mapped to a line with slope multiplied by the scale factor
is mapped to a perpendicular line
is mapped to a parallel line
is mapped onto itself

items.prompt: Dilate the point (9, -4) about the origin with scale factor 3. Give the image.

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Mastery check. Work without help, then stop and hand this section in.

items.prompt: A figure is dilated so that a side of length 6 becomes a side of length 12. What is the scale factor, and what happens to the figure's area?
choices: scale factor 1/2; the area is multiplied by 4
scale factor 2; the area is multiplied by 4
scale factor 2; the area is multiplied by 2
scale factor 6; the area is multiplied by 4
